# Q2 phishing drill results (Example Widgets Inc., synthetic)
We sent a simulated phishing email to all 1,200 staff on 14 May. 9% clicked the link (down from 17% in Q4). 3% entered a password on the fake page (down from 6%). 38% reported the email with the Report button (up from 21%).
Finance and sales had the highest click rates (14% and 12%).
Next: short training for anyone who entered a password; a drill every quarter; the Report button added to the mobile mail app.
mustCover: training for password-enterers, quarterly drills, Report button on mobile

tabs.indepth:
In depth
Fewer staff fell for the fake phishing email, and far more reported it
In May the security team sent all 1,200 staff a simulated phishing email: a harmless fake of the kind attackers send to steal passwords. 9% clicked its link, down from 17% last winter, and 3% typed a password into the fake page, down from 6%.
[Glossary] phishing: An email that pretends to come from someone trusted to trick you into clicking a link or giving away a password.
[Glossary] simulated phishing: A harmless fake phishing email sent by your own security team to measure and train staff.
Reporting is the number that improved most
38% of staff used the Report button, up from 21%. Reports matter because one early report lets the security team pull a real phishing email from every inbox.
[Chart] Clicks halved while reports nearly doubled
Share of staff, %
Category | Q4 | Q2
Clicked | 17 | 9
Entered password | 6 | 3
Reported | 21 | 38
Where the risk remains
Finance and sales clicked most (14% and 12%), likely because they handle invoices and outside contacts every day.
What happens next
Anyone who entered a password gets short training; drills move to every quarter; the Report button comes to the mobile mail app.

tabs.eli5:
ELI5
The big idea: fewer people got fooled, and more people told on the trickster
The security team sent a pretend trick email to everyone, like a fire drill for email. This time fewer people clicked it: about 1 in 11, instead of about 1 in 6 before.
Telling someone is the best move
More people pressed the Report button. That is like shouting "fire!" early: once one person reports a bad email, the team can remove it for everyone.
Who needs extra practice
People in finance and sales clicked most, so they will get a bit more practice.
Think of it like
A fire drill: nobody is in danger, but it shows who knows where the exits are.
